```{r}
# Beginning with head and tail of data

clean_data <- read.csv("Cleaned_Commute.csv")

head(clean_data)
tail(clean_data)
```

```{r}
# Random slice of 6 rows from data frame. Seed used to ensure reproducibility

set.seed(723)

clean_data |>
slice_sample(n = 6)
```

```{r}
clean_data |>
  glimpse()
```

```{r}
clean_data |>
  summary()
```

```{r}
# Confirming categories align with expected n

count(commute_clean, Mode)
count(commute_clean, Gender)
n_distinct(commute_clean$Geography)
```

```{r}
# Visualizing totals for each province 

summary(commute_clean$Total)
ggplot(commute_clean, aes(x = Total)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20)
```

```{r}
# Transit share by province, men vs. women
transit_eda <- commute_clean |> 
  filter(Mode == "Public transit")

nrow(transit_eda) # should be 26
```
```{r}
ggplot(transit_eda, aes(x = Percent, y = fct_reorder(Geography, Percent), 
                        colour = Gender)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("Women+" = "#6CCED9", "Men+" = "#EC9C3E")) +
  labs(
    title = "What Does the Distribution of Transit Users Look Like Across 
    Canadian Provinces and Territories?", 
    x = "Commuters using public transit (%)", 
    y = "Canadian Provinces & Territories") + 
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")) 
```

```{r}
# Visualizing gender gap (Women+ minus Men+) by province 

gap <- gap |>
  mutate(direction = if_else(gap > 0, "Women+ higher", "Men+ higher"))

ggplot(gap, aes(x = gap, y = fct_reorder(Geography, gap), fill = direction)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Women+ higher" = "#6CCED9", "Men+ higher" = "#EC9C3E")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Is There a Gender Gap in Canadian Transit Use?", 
    x = "Gap in percentage points (Women+ minus Men+)",
    y = "Canadian Provinces & Territories",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")) 
```
```{r}
# Creating a list of province/territory abbreviations for following graph's 
# labels (to reduce clutter)

prov_abbr <- c(
  "Newfoundland and Labrador" = "NL", 
  "Prince Edward Island" = "PEI", 
  "Nova Scotia" = "NS", 
  "New Brunswick" = "NB", 
  "Quebec" = "QC", 
  "Ontario" = "ON", 
  "Manitoba" = "MB", 
  "Saskatchewan" = "SK", 
  "Alberta" = "AB", 
  "British Columbia" = "BC", 
  "Yukon" = "YT", 
  "Northwest Territories" = "NWT", 
  "Nunavut" = "NU"
)
```

```{r}
# Does a place's size relate to its share?
ggplot(transit_eda, aes(x = Total, y = Percent, colour = Gender)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = \(x) prov_abbr[x]) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = unname(prov_abbr[Geography])),
                size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Women+" = "#6CCED9", "Men+" = "#EC9C3E")) + 
  labs(
    title = "Does a Province/Territory Size Relate to its Share of Commuters?", 
    x = "Total commuters (log scale)", 
    y = "Commuters using public transit (%)", 
    colour = "Gender"
  ) + 
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")) 
```
